messages.subject: tileMethylCounts running >1 day
parts:
Hi,

I have 20 individual samples of RRBS data that cover ~ 600k CG each.  I have been running tileMethylCounts with 100bp window and 100bp step size and it's been running for > 1 day.  I was wondering if there was an option to speed up this step by using multiple-cores that I am not seeing?

Thanks!

You can try GenomicRanges::tileGenome() function with cut.last.tile.in.chrom=TRUE argument and feed the resulting object to regionCounts(). If making tiles is the slow part it this could make it faster.

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] tileMethylCounts running >1 day
parts:
you can try to use tileMethylCounts2() function below, it could be faster. Warning, I didn't properly test it. If it fails you might have to debug it and change the code

```
setGeneric("tileMethylCounts2", function(object,win.size=1000,step.size=1000,cov.bases=0)
                   standardGeneric("tileMethylCounts2") )


setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRaw"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){
            
            g.meth =as(object,"GRanges")
            #chrs   =IRanges::levels(seqnames(g.meth))
            chrs   =as.character(unique(seqnames(g.meth)))
            #widths =seqlengths(g.meth) # this doesn't work with BioC 3.0
            grl=split(g.meth, seqnames(g.meth))
            max.length =max(end( grl  ))
            numTiles=floor(  (max.length-(win.size-step.size) )/step.size )+1
            
            starts=unlist(sapply(numTiles,function(x) 1+0:(x-1)*step.size ))
            all.wins=GRanges(seqnames=Rle(chrs,numTiles),
                              ranges=IRanges(start=starts,
                                             width=rep(win.size,length(starts))) )
            
            

            regionCounts(object,all.wins,cov.bases,strand.aware=FALSE)
          }
)

#' @aliases tileMethylCounts,methylRawList-method
#' @rdname tileMethylCounts-methods
setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRawList"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){
            
            new.list=lapply(object,tileMethylCounts2,win.size,step.size,cov.bases) 
            new("methylRawList", new.list,treatment=object@treatment)
            
          })

```

If making tiles is the slow part it this could make it faster.

Thanks so much for your help.  We were able to make things work with a modification of the code you sent.  I have another question though, I ran percMethylation on the tiles and I am getting proportions >1.  Should I not be using this command with the tiles? 

Here is the code I ran to get the tiles:

# Function
tileit <- function(object, win.size=100, step.size=100, cov.bases=20) {
  g.meth <- as(object,"GRanges")
  chrs <- as.character(unique(seqnames(g.meth)))
  grl <- split(g.meth, seqnames(g.meth))
  max.length <- max(end(grl))
  numTiles <- floor((max.length - (win.size - step.size))/step.size) + 1
  starts <- unlist(sapply(numTiles,function(x) 1+0:(x-1)*step.size))
  ranges <- IRanges(start=starts, width=rep(win.size,length(starts)))
  all.wins <- GRanges(seqnames=Rle(chrs, numTiles), ranges=ranges)
  rcounts <- regionCounts(object, all.wins, 0, strand.aware=FALSE)
  rcounts.filtered <- rcounts[rcounts$coverage >= cov.bases, ]
  return(rcounts.filtered)
}

# Code to run function on methylKitList
new.list <- lapply(myobj, tileit)
myobj.tiled <- new("methylRawList", new.list, treatment=myobj@treatment)
On Thursday, October 22, 2015 at 2:23:27 PM UTC-7, Altuna Akalin wrote:

you can try to use tileMethylCounts2() function below, it could be faster. Warning, I didn't properly test it. If it fails you might have to debug it and change the code

```
setGeneric("tileMethylCounts2", function(object,win.size=1000,step.size=1000,cov.bases=0)
                   standardGeneric("tileMethylCounts2") )


setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRaw"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){
            
            g.meth =as(object,"GRanges")
            #chrs   =IRanges::levels(seqnames(g.meth))
            chrs   =as.character(unique(seqnames(g.meth)))
            #widths =seqlengths(g.meth) # this doesn't work with BioC 3.0
            grl=split(g.meth, seqnames(g.meth))
            max.length =max(end( grl  ))
            numTiles=floor(  (max.length-(win.size-step.size) )/step.size )+1
            
            starts=unlist(sapply(numTiles,function(x) 1+0:(x-1)*step.size ))
            all.wins=GRanges(seqnames=Rle(chrs,numTiles),
                              ranges=IRanges(start=starts,
                                             width=rep(win.size,length(starts))) )
            
            

            regionCounts(object,all.wins,cov.bases,strand.aware=FALSE)
          }
)

#' @aliases tileMethylCounts,methylRawList-method
#' @rdname tileMethylCounts-methods
setMethod("tileMethylCounts2", signature(object="methylRawList"),
          function(object,win.size,step.size,cov.bases){
            
            new.list=lapply(object,tileMethylCounts2,win.size,step.size,cov.bases) 
            new("methylRawList", new.list,treatment=object@treatment)
            
          })

```
On Thu, Oct 22, 2015 at 10:29 PM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:

We run a for loop that loops over the chromosomes to get the regions to be summarized, then call the function regionCounts(). You can try GenomicRanges::tileGenome() function with cut.last.tile.in.chrom=TRUE argument and feed the resulting object to regionCounts(). If making tiles is the slow part it this could make it faster.

Best,
Altuna
On Thu, Oct 22, 2015 at 9:52 PM, Mac <macg...@gmail.com> wrote:

I also wanted to mention that I also tried to run it with 1000 bp window and step sizes and I think there were ~86,000 tiles (I didn't save it, unfortunately).  Is there an issue with setting the window size so small? I am trying to reproduce a method from this paper: http://nar.oxfordjournals.org/content/early/2015/01/10/nar.gku1386.full where 100bp tiles were used.
On Wednesday, October 21, 2015 at 9:56:49 AM UTC-7, Mac wrote:
There are almost 79,000 scaffolds in this draft genome
On Wed, Oct 21, 2015 at 9:46 AM, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:

How many scaffolds do you have ? More precisely how many unique names are there in the Chr column


On Wednesday, 21 October 2015, Mac <macg...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

I ran one sample and it finished sometime overnight >3hrs.  There is definitely something wrong with what I am doing though.  The methylRaw object only has one row and it says coverage is 922087 (the mean coverage is 78 for this sample).  

Maybe you can see an issue with the upstream commands?  I usually run the pipeline command with 20 samples, but here for the test I only did 1 sample.  I also attached the coverage file that is referenced.

Thanks in advance!

> file.list <- list("Sp3_cat_cov10.txt")
> myobj<-read( file.list,pipeline=list(fraction=TRUE,chr.col=2,start.col=3,end.col=3,
+                                      coverage.col=5,strand.col=4,freqC.col=6 ),
+              sample.id=list("3natural"),assembly="French",
+              treatment=c(0))
> tilemeth<-tileMethylCounts(myobj,win.size=100,step.size=100,cov.bases=20)
> tilemeth

--------------
sample.id: 3natural 
assembly: French 
context: CpG 
resolution: region 

treament: 0 

On Tuesday, October 20, 2015 at 10:21:18 AM UTC-7, Altuna Akalin wrote:

Hi, it shouldn't take this long for 600k CGs, how long does it take it to run on one sample and how many tiles you get?

Best,
Altuna
On Tue, Oct 20, 2015 at 6:50 PM, Mac <macg...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi,

I have 20 individual samples of RRBS data that cover ~ 600k CG each.  I have been running tileMethylCounts with 100bp window and 100bp step size and it's been running for > 1 day.  I was wondering if there was an option to speed up this step by using multiple-cores that I am not seeing?

Thanks!
